topComments.author: EGreg
topComments.text: "Every request spawns a fresh process. Deploying a new version is replacing one file. That means no server restart and no downtime. New requests simply pick up the new binary." I think that's why FastCGI exists. It is the equivalent of PHP's "Swoole" or "FrankenPHP" or "amphp" or Laravel's "octane", etc. Each process is long-lived and tries to clean up its state as much as possible between requests. Forking a new process can take around 8ms ( https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=19005586 ) When I was building https://github.com/Qbix/webserver in PHP, I was faced with forking a new process per request. I implemented fork-per-request at first, similar to PHP-FPM and then implemented the "FastCGI" approach of long-lived processes that clean up after each request. (Modern PHP has introspection so the engine can know what to clean up, before calling the php files to handle things.) However, some things are not really possible to completely reset in PHP, and you have to be careful with database connection pools, etc. Typically those are left open even by preforking processes like php-fpm. Anyway, I ended up flipping it: use the "FastCGI" approach as a default, and if the original PHP code doesn't work (rare), then for that app, you can choose the regular CGI approach of forking a process per request. That way you get maximum speed by default, and manually opt into safety (this is an exception to my usual priorities). PHP is actually quite fast. But I was also interested in transpiling it to C. So I built the transpiler at: https://ulanguage.org/playground ... used Claude to transform about 1000 PHP functions to their native equivalents, but if you use any of the others, it would hook into the Zend runtime and link with it. (There are some nuances with zvals and objects, and resources in previous PHP versions, but I managed to overcome them.) By the way, it also works with Node and Python FFI the same way. You can basically now take PHP, Python or Javascript/Typescript code, and speed up the CPU-bound parts about 10-50x. A lot of that is because of string and JSON handling. Many web apps use strings and JSON a lot. So underneath, I had the compiler use "ropes" for the strings, and avoid concatenation. It also parallelizes the JSON encode and decode into code that can run on multiple cores at once, i.e. large JSON payloads are encoded and decoded in parallel. Those are just huge speedups. Anyway... all of this is mostly focused on speed optimization, so you can solve the literally C100K problem (forget C10K) today, on a regular box. If you don't need speed or FastCGI, your approach is fast enough for the vast majority of applications. PS: By the way, if you fork after your program already loaded the framework and initialized the configuration, then you can run a lot more workers, literally 10x-100x more of them, because Linux and Mac will share all the loaded memory between processes, and do Copy-On-Write only on dirty pages. And when your request is done, and the process exits, that custom memory is efficiently cleaned up by the OS. It is this feature that allowed me to finally get the best of both worlds... run all existing PHP code, that makes blocking I/O requests all over the place to the database, filesystem, network etc. while at the same time being able to handle 100,000 requests in flight at the same time! Swoole and FrankenPHP can't do that.

It gives average speeds in km/h from various length and time units. // Runner A : 1.6 km in 4 minutes Speed averageSpeedA = new Speed(1.6, KILOMETRE, 4.0, MINUTE); averageSpeedA.convert(HOUR); LOGGER.info("Runner A : {}", averageSpeedA); // 24 km/h assertEquals(24.0, averageSpeedA.speed(), 0.001); // Marathonian B : 42 km in 2.25 h Length distanceB = new Length(KILOMETRE, 42.0); Speed averageSpeedB = new Speed(distanceB.length(), KILOMETRE, 2.25, HOUR); LOGGER.info("Marathonian B : {}", averageSpeedB); // 18.667 km/h assertEquals(18.666, averageSpeedB.speed(), 0.001); But I'd like this program being written like: Speed averageSpeedA = 1.6 km / 4.0 min; averageSpeedA.convert(HOUR); Length distanceB = 42.0 km; Speed averageSpeedB = distanceB / 2.25 h; (units of measure symbols are expected sufficient (for a while at least) to discriminate enough the type of object requested to carry a value) This I guess I can perform with the help of: Creating a specific Compiler Plugin, such as shown here . Generate a part of Java code to compile, handling operators and units of measure with AntLR. Is that theoretically possible, reachable with some work, or is this a false trail?

stackOverflowQuestions.title: Visual Studio 2026 Copilot automatically opens multiple Markdown preview tabs
stackOverflowQuestions.bodyExcerpt: I'm experiencing an issue in Visual Studio 2026 (Version 18.10.1) where GitHub Copilot occasionally opens multiple Markdown (.md) files in Preview tabs without any interaction from me. These appear to be planning documents from previous Copilot sessions. The tabs open automatically while I'm working, sometimes filling the editor with multiple tabs and interrupting my workflow. I've looked through Tools → Options for a setting that would prevent Copilot from automatically opening these files, but haven't found anything relevant. My question: Is there a setting in Visual Studio 2026 to prevent Copilot from automatically opening Markdown preview tabs, or is this a known issue?

infoqArticles.description: Spotify reports that AI-assisted development more than doubled monthly merged changes, prompting a review of quality and reliability controls across its engineering organization. infoqArticles.author: Leela Kumili

infoqArticles.title: Article: When Should You Use Liquid Clustering? Benchmarking Lakehouse Layout Strategies
infoqArticles.description: Physical data layout is one of the most consequential decisions in lakehouse engineering. The author compares Liquid Clustering, ZOrdering, and partitioning across four workload types on Delta Lake, uncovering two undocumented failure modes that likely affect production systems today and offering a decision framework for choosing the right layout strategy. By Kushal Kumar Vishwakarma
infoqArticles.author: Kushal Kumar Vishwakarma

infoqArticles.title: Podcast: What Does It Really Mean To Program With AI: A Conversation with Joy Ebertz

This task becomes particularly important as the nature of artificial intelligence changes the landscape of software development. By Joy Ebe
infoqArticles.author: Joy Ebertz

infoqArticles.title: Presentation: You Can't Trust Your AI Bill. And Neither Can I
infoqArticles.description: Erik Peterson discusses why AI spend is eclipsing cloud bills, triggering a major software engineering cost crisis. He explains tokenmaxxing, unit economics, forced developer promotions, and why fully autonomous AI will write, deploy, and govern code by 2028. By Erik Peterson
infoqArticles.author: Erik Peterson

infoqArticles.title: React 19.3: Adds a browser() API, Giving Client-Only Rendering a First-Class Name
infoqArticles.description: React 19.3 was released on September 9, introducing several features including the react-dom browser() API. This API allows components to opt out of server-side rendering, addressing issues with components that rely on client-specific data. It provides a cleaner solution for managing hydration mismatches and supports conditional data fetching, enhancing flexibility for developers. By Daniel Curtis
infoqArticles.author: Daniel Curtis

infoqArticles.title: Java News Roundup: Grails 8, Open Liberty, GlassFish, Infinispan, LangChain4j, Spock

infoqArticles.title: GitLab 19.4 Adds Goal-Driven Agents and Tighter Cost Controls

infoqArticles.author: Matt Saunders

infoqArticles.title: Xcode 27.2 Introduces an Agent- and Merge-Friendly JSON Format for Project Configuration
infoqArticles.description: Apple is introducing a new JSON-based format for Xcode project configuration files, replacing the traditional property-list-based format. Available in Xcode 27.2, the new format aims to improve readability, simplify maintenance, and make project configuration easier for AI coding agents to understand and modify. By Sergio De Simone
infoqArticles.author: Sergio De Simone

infoqArticles.title: Context Language Models: Self-Managing Context to Improve Performance and Reduce Compute Costs
infoqArticles.description: Researchers from Meta, MIT, and the University of Washington introduce Context Language Models (CLMs), a new approach that enables language models to manage and edit their own context rather than relying on predefined mechanisms for summarization, compression, and information retrieval, reporting substantial gains in both performance and computational efficiency. By Sergio De Simone
infoqArticles.author: Sergio De Simone

infoqArticles.author: Matt Saunders

infoqArticles.title: AWS Introduces Enhanced Custom Event Buses for EventBridge

By Renato Losio
infoqArticles.author: Renato Losio

infoqArticles.title: Cloudflare Traces Turns the Proxy Layer into OpenTelemetry Spans, with New Volume-Based Pricing
infoqArticles.description: Cloudflare has put Traces into open beta, extending automatic tracing from Workers to security rules, transformations, cache, routing and origin handling as OpenTelemetry spans. Traces accept and forward W3C traceparent headers, and Trace Rules allow targeted sampling. Pricing moves to ingestion and retention volume from December 1. By Steef-Jan Wiggers
infoqArticles.author: Steef-Jan Wiggers

infoqArticles.title: Android Bench 2 Adds Support for Long-Horizon Tasks, Agentic Evaluation, and Continuous Scoring
infoqArticles.description: Google has released Android Bench 2.0, a major update to its benchmark framework for evaluating AI models and agents on Android development tasks. The update introduces long-horizon tasks (LHTs), agent-based evaluation, and continuous scoring to better assess performance on complex, multi-step development tasks. By Sergio De Simone
infoqArticles.author: Sergio De Simone

infoqArticles.title: Shopify Upgrades Checkout Blocks to Polaris Web Components, Cutting Bundle Sizes up to 85%
